chapter_name: Research methods, evidence-based practice, statistics and critical appraisal 1
chapter_title: Research methods, evidence-based practice, statistics and critical appraisal 1

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding relative risk?

options.text: It is also called risk ratio
It compares the risk of disease and death in two groups
The 'exposed' group is the group of prime interest
The 'unexposed' group is the comparison group
A relative risk greater than 1.0 indicates a decreased risk for the 'exposed' group

correct_answer.text: A relative risk greater than 1.0 indicates a decreased risk for the 'exposed' group

correct_answers.text: A relative risk greater than 1.0 indicates a decreased risk for the 'exposed' group

questions.explanation: Relative risk compares the risk of some health-related event, such as a disease or death, in two groups. The group of primary interest is labelled the exposed group and the comparison group is labelled the unexposed group. The relative risk is calculated according to the following equation: Relative risk = risk of exposed group / risk of unexposed group. A risk ratio of 1.0 indicates identical risks in the two groups. A risk ratio greater than 1.0 indicates an increased risk for the exposed group and a risk ratio less than 1.0 indicates a decreased risk for the exposed group.

questions.question_text: If... A = number of people with disease and exposure B = number of people without disease but with exposure C = number of people with disease but without exposure D = number of people without disease and without exposure, which of the following equations will calculate the odds ratio?

options.text: AB divided by CD
AC divided by BD
AA divided by BD
AD divided by BC
ABD divided by ACB

correct_answer.text: AD divided by BC

correct_answers.text: AD divided by BC

questions.explanation: Odds ratio is a measure of association that qualifies the relationship between an exposure and health outcome for a comparative study. The odds ratio is also sometimes called the cross-product ratio, as it is obtained by the product of the number of diseased people with exposure and the number of healthy people without exposure divided by the product of healthy people with exposure and diseased people without exposure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding a placebo drug used in a clinical trial?

options.text: It has no effect
It is pharmacologically inert
It is identical in appearance to the active drug
The person administering the drug is blinded
It should be given with as much confidence as the active drug

correct_answer.text: It has no effect

correct_answers.text: It has no effect

questions.explanation: The placebo drugs, although pharmacologically inert, do produce effects, as reported by the participants of the trial.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is least likely to influence the placebo effect of a particular drug?

options.text: Size of the tablet
Colour of the tablet
Status of the person administering the drug
Age of the patient
Expectation of the patient

correct_answer.text: Age of the patient

correct_answers.text: Age of the patient

questions.explanation: The placebo effect is least likely to be influenced by the age of the patient.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding measures of central location?

options.text: They are a range of values that best represent a characteristic of a group of individuals
They are a single value that best represent a characteristic of a group of individuals
They are a measure that quantifies how much individuals in a group vary from each other
They are a measure that quantifies how much individuals in a group vary from other groups
None of the above

correct_answer.text: They are a single value that best represent a characteristic of a group of individuals

correct_answers.text: They are a single value that best represent a characteristic of a group of individuals

questions.explanation: A measure of central location such as arithmetic mean, median or mode is a single value that best represents a particular characteristic such as age or height of a group of individuals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a measure of central tendency?

options.text: Arithmetic mean
Median
Mode
Range
Mid-range

correct_answer.text: Range

correct_answers.text: Range

questions.explanation: Range is a measure of dispersion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the normal distribution?

options.text: Symmetric
Asymmetric
Skewed
Positively skewed
Negatively skewed

correct_answer.text: Symmetric

correct_answers.text: Symmetric

questions.explanation: The symmetrical clustering of values around a central location is typical of many frequency distributions and is called the normal distribution.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the 'arithmetic mean', except:

options.text: It is a measure of central tendency
It is best suited for data with a normal distribution
It is sensitive to extreme values
It is a good summary measure for skewed data
It is a poor summary measure for skewed data

correct_answer.text: It is a good summary measure for skewed data

correct_answers.text: It is a good summary measure for skewed data

questions.explanation: Arithmetic mean, because of its sensitivity to extreme values, is considered a poor summary measure for data that are severely skewed in either a positive or a negative direction.

questions.question_text: Identify the mode from the following set of values: 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 6, 9.
questions.explanation: Mode is the value that occurs most often in a set of data and in this example the number 1 occurs four times, which is more than any other value.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a measure of dispersion?

options.text: Range
Mid-range
Interquartile range
Variants
Standard deviation

correct_answer.text: Mid-range

correct_answers.text: Mid-range

questions.explanation: Mid-range is a measure of central tendency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding standard deviation?

options.text: It is a measure of dispersion
The square root of variance is standard deviation
It is usually represented by s
It is usually represented by s2
None of the above

correct_answer.text: It is usually represented by s2

correct_answers.text: It is usually represented by s2

questions.explanation: Variance and standard deviation are measures of dispersion. Variance is the mean of the square differences of the observations from the mean. It is usually represented in formulas as s2. The standard deviation is the square root of variance and is usually represented in formulas as s.

questions.question_text: In a distribution that is skewed to the left, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Mean, mode and median are on the same line
Mean is towards the tail
Median is in the middle
Mode is towards the right
Use of median is preferred to represent the centre of the data

correct_answer.text: Mean, mode and median are on the same line

correct_answers.text: Mean, mode and median are on the same line

questions.explanation: Mean, mode and median lie on the same line in symmetrical distribution and not in skewed distribution. In skewed distributions, the median is preferred to represent the centre of the data because it is not affected by a few extremely high or low observations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes a confidence interval?

options.text: It helps to calculate the mean
It helps to calculate the mode
It helps to calculate the median
It is the same as interquartile range
It indicates how precise or imprecise the estimate is

correct_answer.text: It indicates how precise or imprecise the estimate is

correct_answers.text: It indicates how precise or imprecise the estimate is

questions.explanation: A confidence interval indicates how precise or imprecise an estimate is.

questions.question_text: Which of the following measures of central tendency has half of the observations below it and half of the observations above it?

options.text: Arithmetic mean
Geometric mean
Median
Mode
Range

correct_answer.text: Median

correct_answers.text: Median

questions.explanation: The median is at the halfway point of a set of data that have been arranged in rank order.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most commonly used measure of central location?

options.text: Arithmetic mean
Geometric mean
Median
Mode
Range

correct_answer.text: Arithmetic mean

correct_answers.text: Arithmetic mean

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is the most commonly used measure of central location.

questions.question_text: All of the following are measures of dispersion, except:

options.text: Variance
Standard deviation
Range
Percentile
Interquartile range

correct_answer.text: Percentile

correct_answers.text: Percentile

questions.explanation: A percentile is at a particular point in a data set and is not a measure of dispersion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the distribution curve below? Frequency Variable

options.text: Negatively skewed
Positively skewed
Skewed to the left
Normal distribution
None of the above

correct_answer.text: Positively skewed

correct_answers.text: Positively skewed

questions.explanation: This distribution curve is positively skewed as the tail points to the right and defines the direction of the skew.

questions.question_text: Which of the following measures of central location is most affected by extreme values?

options.text: Range
Mode
Median
Geometric mean
Arithmetic mean

correct_answer.text: Arithmetic mean

correct_answers.text: Arithmetic mean

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is most sensitive to extreme values.

questions.question_text: Which of the following data sets has the smallest standard deviation?
questions.explanation: As all the observations have the same value, the mean is 30, the difference between each value and the mean is 0 and thus the standard deviation is also 0. In other words, there is no dispersion from the mean.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is essential for testing the effectiveness of a given treatment?

options.text: Untreated controls
Double-blind procedure
A valid measure of change
Patients' self-reports
Physiological measures

correct_answer.text: A valid measure of change

correct_answers.text: A valid measure of change

questions.explanation: A validated instrument to measure a change is essential for testing the effectiveness of a given treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not typically included in a study protocol?

options.text: Aims of the study
Review of relevant literature
Study design
Anticipated date of the start of the study
Anticipated date of the publication of results

correct_answer.text: Anticipated date of the publication of results

correct_answers.text: Anticipated date of the publication of results

questions.explanation: The anticipated date and place of publication of the results is usually not included in a study protocol.

questions.question_text: All of the following are essential qualities of a well designed study, except:

options.text: Clearly defined inclusion and exclusion criteria
Power calculation
Use of reliable and valid instruments
Excluding the data from drop-outs to avoid spurious results
Intention-to-treat analysis

correct_answer.text: Excluding the data from drop-outs to avoid spurious results

correct_answers.text: Excluding the data from drop-outs to avoid spurious results

questions.explanation: The data from drop-outs should always be included in an intention-to-treat analysis.

questions.question_text: Placebo-controlled studies are justifiable in which of the following scenarios?

options.text: When a new drug is developed
To measure mortality risk
To convince people to use a new drug
When there is no possibility of treatment being better than placebo
When there is genuine uncertainty as to whether the treatment is better than placebo

correct_answer.text: When there is genuine uncertainty as to whether the treatment is better than placebo

correct_answers.text: When there is genuine uncertainty as to whether the treatment is better than placebo

questions.explanation: A placebo-controlled study can be justifiable only if there is genuine uncertainty as to whether the active treatment is better than placebo.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding data collection?

options.text: Questionnaires sent by mail usually get a response rate of less than 40%
The maximum amount of data should be collected from the records
The General Health Questionnaire (GHQ) can be used to screen for psychosis
The Present State Examination is a structured interview for mental state examination
The Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (SADS) is a structured interview

correct_answer.text: The Present State Examination is a structured interview for mental state examination

correct_answers.text: The Present State Examination is a structured interview for mental state examination

questions.explanation: The Present State Examination is a structured mental state interview. The response rates to mail questionnaires are usually between 40 and 60%. The GHQ is a screening instrument for non-psychotic illness and the SADS is a semi-structured interview.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding study designs?

options.text: Observation studies can be used to establish the direction of causality
Case-control studies give information about prevalence
Case-control studies give information about incidence
Sex cannot be a confounder
Cohort studies provide information about relative risk

correct_answer.text: Cohort studies provide information about relative risk

correct_answers.text: Cohort studies provide information about relative risk

questions.explanation: Cohort studies do provide information about relative risk, which is the ratio of illness rates in the exposed to the unexposed. Observational studies can provide clues only to causality but they cannot establish the direction of causality. Case-control studies give clues to aetiology. Sex can be confounding as it is a variable related to both risk factors and illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding research data?

options.text: It is conventional to report 90% confidence intervals
In normal distribution, the probability of the population mean lying more than two standard errors away from the sample mean is less than 5%
Confidence intervals can be calculated from the mean and standard error only if the variable is assumed to be normally distributed
The standard error of the mean enables estimation of the range within which the mean would fall if the study were repeated
The standard error of the mean is a function of the standard deviation of the sample and of the sample size

correct_answer.text: It is conventional to report 90% confidence intervals

correct_answers.text: It is conventional to report 90% confidence intervals

questions.explanation: It is conventional to report 95% confidence intervals.

questions.question_text: Type II error is caused by which of the following?

options.text: Non-random recruitment
Too many groups in the study design
Too many subjects
Too few subjects
None of the above

correct_answer.text: Too few subjects

correct_answers.text: Too few subjects

questions.explanation: With too few subjects there is a high risk of type II error or a false negative result.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the principles of meta-analysis?

options.text: All studies should be given equal weight
Double-blind randomized controlled trials are the gold standard
The topic to be reviewed must be clearly defined
Studies published in a wide range of journals should be included
Publication bias can be reduced by using a funnel plot

correct_answer.text: All studies should be given equal weight

correct_answers.text: All studies should be given equal weight

questions.explanation: Larger studies should be given greater weight.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding frequency measures?

options.text: Prevalence rates are a measure of new cases
Incidence can be determined by performing a cross-sectional survey
Incidence is a proportion and can therefore be best expressed as a percentage
With prevalence rates, the denominator is a percentile
Chronic diseases have a low incidence and a high prevalence

correct_answer.text: Chronic diseases have a low incidence and a high prevalence

correct_answers.text: Chronic diseases have a low incidence and a high prevalence

questions.explanation: Incidence is the rate of new cases occurring in a defined population in a given time period, whereas prevalence is the proportion of a defined population that has the disease at a given time. Chronic diseases tend to show higher prevalence figures than incidence as the patient survives for a longer time and the total number of patients is always higher than the number of new cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding statistical power?

options.text: It gives the probability that a type I error will not occur
It depends upon the strength of the expected association in relation to the measurement error
It depends upon the prevalence of the exposure
It depends upon the significance level chosen
It depends upon the sample size

correct_answer.text: It gives the probability that a type I error will not occur

correct_answers.text: It gives the probability that a type I error will not occur

questions.explanation: Statistical power gives the probability that a type II error will not occur. The statistical power increases with increases in b, c, d and e.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding randomized controlled trials?

options.text: A double-blind design eliminates the chance of measurement bias
They are observational studies
They can be thought of as matched cohort studies in which unknown confounders are randomly allocated
Subjects who drop out should be left out of the final analysis
If the randomization is not biased, it is not necessary to analyse the data for potentially confounding variables

correct_answer.text: They can be thought of as matched cohort studies in which unknown confounders are randomly allocated

correct_answers.text: They can be thought of as matched cohort studies in which unknown confounders are randomly allocated

questions.explanation: Blinding can only reduce the chance of measurement bias but cannot eliminate it. Randomized controlled trials are not observational studies but experimental studies. Drop-outs have to be considered in an intention-to-treat analysis. It is important to analyse data for potentially confounding variables as even unbiased randomization can result in differences between the groups.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding confounding variables in epidemiological research, except:

options.text: They can be either a risk factor or a protective factor
They can be associated with both exposure and disease
They can be taken into account by introducing randomization in a study design
They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease
They can be taken into account by introducing matching into a study design

correct_answer.text: They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease

correct_answers.text: They are on the causal pathway between exposure and disease

questions.explanation: The confounding variables are not on the causal pathway between exposure and disease.

questions.question_text: In experimental studies, which of the following is not a form of group comparison?

options.text: Parallel groups
Cross-over design
Double blinding
Factorial design
Sequential design

correct_answer.text: Double blinding

correct_answers.text: Double blinding

questions.explanation: Double blinding is not a form of group comparison but a technique used in randomized controlled trials where the researcher and the subject are blinded from the information about whether the subject is entering the treatment arm or placebo arm of the study. Double blinding helps to prevent observation bias as well as placebo effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods of data collection is the most expensive and time consuming but can generate high-quality data?

options.text: Computer interview
Telephone interview
Mail questionnaires
Personal interview
Record reviews

correct_answer.text: Personal interview

correct_answers.text: Personal interview

questions.explanation: The personal interview approach can generate high-quality data with a high response rate but is expensive and time consuming. It also requires training and practice for the interviewers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding correlation?

options.text: It is a useful technique to analyse nominal data
It usually examines the association between two variables (X and Y)
A 0 correlation means that there is no association between X and Y
A positive correlation means that Y increases in a straight line as X increases
A negative correlation means that Y decreases in a straight line as X increases

correct_answer.text: It is a useful technique to analyse nominal data

correct_answers.text: It is a useful technique to analyse nominal data

questions.explanation: Correlation is used to look at the association between continuous quantitative data.

questions.question_text: What is the range of the correlation coefficient?

options.text: 0 to +1
-1 to 0

questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient ranges from -1 to +1. It is used in research to show the strength of the linear relationship between two variables.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding systematic reviews?

options.text: They deal with a specific research question
They clearly explain the search strategy
They pool the results from the selected studies
They can be valuable for evidence-based practice
Overall conclusions are not more reliable than individual studies

correct_answer.text: Overall conclusions are not more reliable than individual studies

correct_answers.text: Overall conclusions are not more reliable than individual studies

questions.explanation: Systematic reviews are considered the gold-standard source for research evidence and overall conclusions are usually more reliable than those drawn from individual studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following could negatively influence the conclusions of a meta-analysis?

options.text: Combining the results of several studies
Calculation of a P value from the pooled data
Calculation of a confidence interval from the pooled data
Interpretation of the findings
Publication bias

correct_answer.text: Publication bias

correct_answers.text: Publication bias

questions.explanation: Publication bias can have a negative effect on the findings of a meta-analysis. Ideally, a meta-analysis should include all the information provided by all the studies performed to answer a particular question. If the results of only positive studies are considered for meta-analysis, then the findings could be biased towards a particular intervention, as all the negative studies were excluded.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding forest plots?

options.text: They are used to present results of randomized controlled trials only
The studies are listed on the vertical axis
The outcome measure is on the horizontal axis
The 'line of unity' intersects the horizontal axis
The overall outcome is represented by the diamond shape

correct_answer.text: They are used to present results of randomized controlled trials only

correct_answers.text: They are used to present results of randomized controlled trials only

questions.explanation: Forest plots are generally used to present the results of a meta-analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statistical methods is not used to test for heterogeneity?

options.text: Forest plot
Galbraith plot
Z statistic
Chi-square statistic
The Peto method

correct_answer.text: The Peto method

correct_answers.text: The Peto method

questions.explanation: The Peto method is used for individual and combined odds ratios.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best explains the term 'publication bias'?

options.text: Studies with negative findings are more likely to be published
Studies with positive findings are more likely to be published
Studies with high mortality figures are more likely to be published
Studies with low mortality figures are more likely to be published
Studies sponsored by drug companies are more likely to be published

correct_answer.text: Studies with positive findings are more likely to be published

correct_answers.text: Studies with positive findings are more likely to be published

questions.explanation: Publication bias means the studies with positive findings are more likely to be published.

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods can be used to identify publication bias?

options.text: Graphical method
Meta regression
Correlation coefficient
Funnel plots
Forest plots

correct_answer.text: Funnel plots

correct_answers.text: Funnel plots

questions.explanation: Funnel plots are used to identify publication bias. If publication bias is absent, then the funnel plot is symmetrical; it becomes asymmetrical in the presence of publication bias.

questions.question_text: Which of the following study designs would be most suitable for aetiological studies?

options.text: Cross-sectional studies
Case-controlled studies
Randomized controlled trials
Intervention studies
None of the above

correct_answer.text: Case-controlled studies

correct_answers.text: Case-controlled studies

questions.explanation: In case-controlled studies, patients with a particular disease are identified and their past exposure to the aetiological factors is studied and compared with that of control subjects who do not have the disease. The odds ratio is estimated and potential confounding factors are measured.

questions.question_text: Suppose a test on cerebrospinal fluid has been developed to identify depression. Which of the following terms best explains the following situation: 'A patient has been given a negative result when he is actually suffering from depression'?

options.text: True positive
True negative
False negative
False positive
None of the above

correct_answer.text: False negative

correct_answers.text: False negative

questions.explanation: A false-negative result means that a negative result has been shown by the test when the patient is actually suffering from depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the 'positive predictive value' of a screening test?

options.text: The proportion of people getting a positive result who will have the disease
The proportion of people with the disease who test positive
The proportion of people without the disease who test negative
The proportion of people getting a negative result who will not have the disease
The likelihood that those who test positive will have the disease as opposed to not have the disease

correct_answer.text: The proportion of people getting a positive result who will have the disease

correct_answers.text: The proportion of people getting a positive result who will have the disease

questions.explanation: The positive predictive value is the proportion of people scoring positive on the test who will have the disease.

questions.question_text: What is the most suitable study design for assessing the effectiveness of a newly developed treatment?

options.text: Retrospective study
Cross-sectional study
Randomized controlled trial
Observational studies
Systematic review

correct_answer.text: Randomized controlled trial

correct_answers.text: Randomized controlled trial

questions.explanation: Randomized controlled trials are considered the gold standard for assessing the effectiveness of a newly developed intervention.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the term 'number needed to treat'?

options.text: The number of patients needed to be treated for the completion of a particular trial
The number of patients who must be treated with an intervention without experiencing any adverse side-effects
The number of patients who must be treated with a particular intervention for one patient to experience the beneficial effect
It means the same as absolute risk reduction
It means the same as 'number needed to harm'

correct_answer.text: The number of patients who must be treated with a particular intervention for one patient to experience the beneficial effect

correct_answers.text: The number of patients who must be treated with a particular intervention for one patient to experience the beneficial effect

questions.explanation: The number needed to treat is the number of patients who must be treated with an intervention for one patient to experience the benefit of the treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding survival analysis?

options.text: It is usually applicable to longitudinal cohort studies
It looks exclusively at rate and time of death
It can be used to calculate the median survival time
It can be used to predict the likelihood of a number of outcomes in the study group
It is not useful for cross-sectional studies

correct_answer.text: It looks exclusively at rate and time of death

correct_answers.text: It looks exclusively at rate and time of death

questions.explanation: Survival analysis is not exclusively used for information on time to death but can be applied to a number of outcomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best explains the term 'cost-effectiveness analysis'?

options.text: An analysis of an intervention to cut down a cost
An analysis of a number of interventions to cut down the cost
An analysis to compare multiple interventions that produce the same beneficial outcome with a similar degree of benefit
An analysis of the cost of a number of interventions for achieving a particular desired effect
An analysis of multiple interventions to choose the most suitable one for a particular condition

correct_answer.text: An analysis of the cost of a number of interventions for achieving a particular desired effect

correct_answers.text: An analysis of the cost of a number of interventions for achieving a particular desired effect

questions.explanation: Cost-effectiveness analysis is an economic analysis aiming to compare the cost of multiple interventions that achieve the same effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding qualitative research?

options.text: It analyses the quality of data produced by a randomized controlled trial
It looks at the subjective experiences of the participants
It is useful for investigating attitudes and beliefs of the participants
It does not necessarily require a hypothesis at the beginning of the research
The stress is on the quality and depth of information gathered during research

correct_answer.text: It analyses the quality of data produced by a randomized controlled trial

correct_answers.text: It analyses the quality of data produced by a randomized controlled trial

questions.explanation: Qualitative research collects and analyses data that cannot be presented as numbers; it is used in the initial stages of research, studies dealing with attitudes and beliefs, assessment tools development, etc.
